from.description: The id of the one that acts: a person, a system, an app, a store, a component or a piece of infrastructure, at any level.

to.description: The id of the one it acts on: a person, a system, an app, a store, a component or a piece of infrastructure, at any level.

via.description: What the exchange passes through, in order from `from`: pieces of infrastructure, apps, components, systems. Never a store, never an end.

opens.description: `to`: the far side opened the channel this exchange goes down, as when an agent dials out and the server sends down that tunnel: `from` the server, `to` the agent, `opens: to`. The dialling is no connection of its own. Left out when the one that sends opened it, or nobody has said.

access.description: What the connection does to the store it ends at: read, write or read-write. Left out for neither, and for "not said".

name.description: The few words on the arrow, a verb first: one line of 1 to 100 characters. May be left out.

only.description: The condition under which the thing is there at all, begun with "when", "on" or "for", so that it reads after the word "only": `only: when a customer pays by card`. One line of at most 100 characters. Left out when it is always there.

description.description: What passes and why, where the name does not say it, in 1 to 2,000 characters.

technology.description: What the exchange is carried in, such as a protocol or a format: ids of records in technologies/, a set.

source.description: Where the code shows it, a file in which the code or config of `from` names `to`: the paths of one to three files, counted from the folder that holds the model's folder, written with `/`. A path with `..`, with `*` or with `/` at its start is an error, and the check warns when a path is not there or is a folder. When `from` has no code here, the route of `to` that takes its call; from a person, the entry point they use. Left out when nobody has looked.

description: One thing acts on another, for one purpose. It has an id of its own. Two connections may join the same two things, one for each purpose, and `from` and `to` may be one thing, when a part talks to its own copies. C4 calls it a relationship.
